title: Grade 4 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — Mock Exam #11

pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — MOCK EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is one of the five great elements? (1 mark)
   A. Akash
   B. Salt
   C. Metal
   D. Wood

2. Which of these is NOT one of the five elements? (1 mark)
   A. Agni
   B. Vayu
   C. Prithvi
   D. Metal

3. Who was Hiranyakashipu? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A proud and cruel king
   C. A good teacher
   D. A festival

4. Which city did Guru Ram Das Ji start? (1 mark)
   A. Amritsar
   B. Nairobi
   C. Mombasa
   D. Varanasi

5. A snake is often shown with statues of which Tirthankar? (1 mark)
   A. Parshvanath
   B. Guru Ram Das
   C. Narsimha
   D. Buddha

6. What promise lesson do we learn from the Ayodhya Kaand? (1 mark)
   A. Forget promises
   B. Break promises
   C. Promises are for kings only
   D. Keep your promises

7. What is the holy scripture of the Sikhs? (1 mark)
   A. Ramayan
   B. Dhammapada
   C. Kalpasutra
   D. Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji

8. Who took Ram and Lakshman to protect his forest prayers? (1 mark)
   A. Sage Vishwamitra
   B. King Shibi
   C. Sage Valmiki
   D. Guru Nanak

9. What does pita mean in the prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Friend
   B. Wealth
   C. Mother
   D. Father

10. What is darshan? (1 mark)
   A. Running around
   B. Leaving early
   C. Paying fees
   D. Looking at the murti with respect

11. What does Vandana mean? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A tree
   C. A meal
   D. An act of respect and prayer

12. What should you do with your shoes before entering a Mandir? (1 mark)
   A. Wear them
   B. Carry them inside
   C. Throw them
   D. Remove them

13. Which is safe behaviour in a matatu? (1 mark)
   A. Putting the head out of the window
   B. Distracting the driver
   C. Wearing the seat belt
   D. Standing in the aisle

14. What should be written when an item is put in the lost and found? (1 mark)
   A. The price
   B. Nothing
   C. A secret code
   D. The date and the finder's name

15. Who was Bhai Lalo? (1 mark)
   A. A shopkeeper in Nairobi
   B. An honest carpenter in the Guru Nanak story
   C. A king of Ayodhya
   D. A Jain monk

16. Which of these is honest saving? (1 mark)
   A. Taking from another's savings
   B. Hiding others' money
   C. Borrowing secretly
   D. Saving your own money and not taking from others

17. The shopkeeper gives you Ksh 100 in change but you should get Ksh 70. What is the extra amount? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 100
   B. Ksh 30
   C. Ksh 170
   D. Ksh 70

18. What is the lesson of the Harishchandra story? (1 mark)
   A. Promises are not important
   B. Lies are useful
   C. Truth is worth more than wealth or comfort
   D. Wealth is everything

19. What should you wear for yoga? (1 mark)
   A. A raincoat
   B. Tight clothes
   C. Loose and comfortable clothes
   D. Heavy boots

20. How do you sit in Vajra Asana? (1 mark)
   A. Sit cross-legged
   B. Lie down
   C. Stand on your hands
   D. Kneel and sit on your heels

21. Which principle is being followed by greeting parents with Namaste and saying a morning prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Artha only
   B. Punarjanam only
   C. Prarthana and respect for Paramatma
   D. Kama only

22. What does Moksha mean? (1 mark)
   A. A meal
   B. Freedom of the soul
   C. A game
   D. A song

23. Why is prayer a principle of Dharma? (1 mark)
   A. It ends homework
   B. It makes us thankful, calm and humble
   C. It builds houses
   D. It makes us proud

24. What does Maha Shivratri teach? (1 mark)
   A. Playing games all night
   B. Getting rich
   C. Winning arguments
   D. Self-control, faith and staying alert to do good

25. Which Jain scripture is often read during Paryushan? (1 mark)
   A. Guru Granth Sahib
   B. Dhammapada
   C. Kalpasutra
   D. Ramayan

26. Which festival is a national festival? (1 mark)
   A. Paryushan Parva
   B. Madaraka Day
   C. Vasant Panchami
   D. Maha Shivratri

27. How long is Paryushan in one Jain tradition? (1 mark)
   A. Eight days
   B. One year
   C. One month
   D. Two days

28. What is the Indian name for Tuesday? (1 mark)
   A. Shukravaar
   B. Somvaar
   C. Ravivaar
   D. Mangalvaar

29. Which of these is a month of the Indian traditional calendar? (1 mark)
   A. March
   B. Chaitra
   C. June
   D. January

30. The Indian traditional calendar is based on what? (1 mark)
   A. Only the rain
   B. The Moon and the Sun
   C. The school year
   D. Only the stars of the south

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. How can you learn more about the scriptures? Give four ways. (4 marks)

32. Explain how a school can make festivals inclusive. (4 marks)

33. Draw a timeline from January to December and mark Maha Shivratri, Madaraka Day and Paryushan. (4 marks)

34. Who compiled Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji first, and who declared it the eternal Guru? (2 marks)

35. Write a weekly plan using English and Indian day names with one activity for each of three days. (5 marks)

36. Give four roles of sacred plants. (4 marks)

37. Give two of Parshvanath's four rules. (2 marks)

38. Explain what the Sigalovada Sutta teaches about the six directions. (3 marks)

39. Describe the four things a person may do at a Mandir and what each shows. (4 marks)

40. Describe the lessons of the Uttaradhyayan Sutra. (4 marks)

41. Describe an experiment to show that plants need water. (4 marks)

42. Explain what the white colour, the veena and the book stand for in the picture of Saraswati. (3 marks)

43. Explain what we learn from the lives of any two Enlightened Beings. (4 marks)

44. Distinguish between Madaraka Day and Jamhuri Day. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — MOCK EXAM #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Akash
   The five elements are Prithvi, Jal, Agni, Vayu and Akash.

2. D — Metal
   The five are earth, water, fire, air and space.

3. B — A proud and cruel king
   He was Prahlad's proud father.

4. A — Amritsar
   The city that grew into Amritsar.

5. A — Parshvanath
   The snake is a sign of Parshvanath.

6. D — Keep your promises
   Ram kept his father's promise.

7. D — Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji
   Sikhs follow it as their eternal Guru.

8. A — Sage Vishwamitra
   Vishwamitra asked for their help.

9. D — Father
   Pita means father.

10. D — Looking at the murti with respect
   Darshan is a respectful sight of God.

11. D — An act of respect and prayer
   Vandana is respectful prayer.

12. D — Remove them
   Shoes are removed to keep it clean and show respect.

13. C — Wearing the seat belt
   A seat belt protects you.

14. D — The date and the finder's name
   The book keeps a record.

15. B — An honest carpenter in the Guru Nanak story
   Bhai Lalo earned by honest work.

16. D — Saving your own money and not taking from others
   Honest saving respects others.

17. B — Ksh 30
   100 minus 70 is 30.

18. C — Truth is worth more than wealth or comfort
   The king chose truth.

19. C — Loose and comfortable clothes
   Loose clothes help us move.

20. D — Kneel and sit on your heels
   You sit on your heels.

21. C — Prarthana and respect for Paramatma
   Prayer and respect for God.

22. B — Freedom of the soul
   Moksha is the highest goal.

23. B — It makes us thankful, calm and humble
   Prayer helps us feel calm.

24. D — Self-control, faith and staying alert to do good
   These are its lessons.

25. C — Kalpasutra
   Many Jains hear the Kalpasutra.

26. B — Madaraka Day
   It is celebrated by all Kenyans.

27. A — Eight days
   Eight days in one tradition and ten in another.

28. D — Mangalvaar
   Mangal is Mars.

29. B — Chaitra
   Chaitra is the first month.

30. B — The Moon and the Sun
   It is lunar and solar.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Listen to a resource person, visit a temple or library, discuss with friends, watch a documentary, use a safe search engine with an adult (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Give clear instructions, help learners with special needs to take part, share food and clothes with the needy, and invite all faiths and communities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: A line from January to December with Maha Shivratri in February or March, Madaraka Day on 1 June and Paryushan in August or September.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the line and months, 1 mark for each correct festival.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Guru Arjan Dev Ji compiled it; Guru Gobind Singh Ji declared it the Guru.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each name.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any correct plan, for example Somvaar: help at home; Guruvaar: thank a teacher; Shukravaar: share with a friend.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the format and 1 mark each for three correct day names with activities.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: They give oxygen and clean the air; they give shade for rest and prayer; their leaves, fruits and bark are used for food and medicine; their leaves and flowers are used in worship; they remind us to care for life.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct role.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya or Aparigraha (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rule.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: It tells us to respect and care for parents, teachers, family, friends, workers and helpers, and holy teachers, and they in turn care for us.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming groups, 1 mark for respect and care, 1 mark for mutual duty.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Darshan shows respect, aarti offers light, prasad shows blessing and sharing, bhajans show love in song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Practise Ahimsa, be honest, control greed and anger, and respect teachers (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Plant bean seeds in two tins of soil. Water one tin every day and give none to the other. Compare them after one and two weeks. The watered seeds sprout and grow but the dry seeds do not.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two tins, 1 mark for different watering, 1 mark for comparing over time, 1 mark for the result.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: White stands for purity and peace, the veena stands for music and the arts, and the book stands for knowledge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct meaning.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any two, for example: from Prahlad's story that faith and honesty can defeat pride, and from Siddhartha that we must be kind to hurt animals.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each being with a correct lesson.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Madaraka Day is 1 June and marks internal self-government in 1963. Jamhuri Day is 12 December and marks independence in 1963 and the republic in 1964.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each date and 1 mark for a difference.
